mainTopic: The source for the עומר permitting rooted grain, the rules of reaping before the עומר, and the practices of the people of יריחו
overview: The amud opens by searching for the source of the משנה's rule that the עומר permits even grain that has only taken root. רבי יאשיה, שמואל and רבי יצחק each suggest a word in a פסוק (אביב, מהחל חרמש, קמה), and each proof is pushed off to a later stage of growth. רבא finally proves it from אשר תזרע בשדה: 'which you sow' reaches back to the earliest stage, and 'in the field' limits it to grain that has rooted. A new משנה follows. It lists cases where grain may be reaped before the עומר: irrigated valley fields, fodder, saplings, a house of mourning and the בית המדרש. It also gives the ideal and the fallback ways to harvest the עומר itself. The גמרא uses רבי בנימין's reading of two phrases in one פסוק to show that only fields fit for the עומר are restricted. With help from רבי יוחנן, it shows the split is by type of field, not by type of grain. Finally, it identifies the יריחו line of the משנה as רבי יהודה's. It then challenges that from a ברייתא in which רבי יהודה says none of יריחו's practices were approved, only some were not protested. The list of protested practices continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יאשיה is pressed for the source of the rooting rule
steps.stepSummary: Someone urgently asks רבי יאשיה to find a source for the משנה's rule that the עומר permits grain that has only taken root.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone said to רבי יאשיה of his generation: Don't settle down until you explain to me this line of the משנה. Where do we learn that the עומר permits grain once it has taken root?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a sharp request: find the source for the משנה's rule that the עומר permits even grain that has just taken root. This sets up the search for a פסוק in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says new grain becomes permitted through the עומר even if it had only taken root before the עומר was brought. That is a surprising rule, since the grain was barely growing at that point. So someone demands a source for it in the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking root; the earliest stage of growth after planting
The barley offering brought on the 16th of ניסן, which permits eating the new crop
Literally 'don't sit on your knees'; don't rest until you finish
Of his generation; a later sage, not the earlier תנא with the same name

phrases.english: to Rabbi Yoshiya of his generation:
Do not sit on your knees
phrases.notes: He means: don't settle down or rest yet.

phrases.english: until you have explained this mishna:
From where do we know that the omer permits grain upon its taking root?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֵּיתֵב אַכַּרְעָיךָ עַד דִּמְפָרְשַׁתְּ לֵיהּ לְהָא מַתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a search for the source of the משנה's rule
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that the עומר permits grain that has only taken root

steps.title: רבי יאשיה learns it from the word אביב
steps.stepSummary: רבי יאשיה answers from the word אביב. Saying the offering must be ripe grain implies there is grain that is not yet ripe, and the עומר still permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do we learn it? The פסוק says 'אביב', ripe grain. Doesn't that imply there is grain that is not אביב, which the עומר still permits?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יאשיה answers with a פסוק. Because the offering itself must be אביב, there must also be less-developed grain that is not אביב. He says that grain is still permitted by the עומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic is 'מכלל', learning by implication. If the תורה needs to say the offering must come from ripe grain, then there is also grain at an earlier stage. רבי יאשיה wants that earlier stage to be grain that has only taken root.

keyTerms.meaning: Ripe grain in the ear; the grain the עומר is brought from
Does this not imply? A way of learning by implication

phrases.english: From where do we derive it?
As it is written: "grain in the ear"
Does this not imply that there is grain that is not "grain in the ear"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 1
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word אביב implies there is unripe grain, including rooted grain, that the עומר permits

steps.title: Maybe the implied grain reached one-third
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The grain that is 'not אביב' could be grain that has already grown one-third, not grain that has only taken root.
steps.simpleTranslation: It might mean grain that is not אביב but has actually reached one-third of its growth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי יאשיה's proof. The grain that is 'not אביב' might be at a middle stage, one-third grown, and not just taking root.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inference proves only that some earlier stage is permitted. It does not prove which stage. Since one-third growth is also 'not אביב', the פסוק does not prove the משנה's rule about taking root.

keyTerms.meaning: One-third; grain that has reached a third of its full growth
But really; introduces the other way to read the case

phrases.english: It could be grain that is not "grain in the ear",
but it actually reached one-third of its growth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 2
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the use of אביב as a source for the rooting rule
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The inference could refer to grain that is one-third grown, not grain that has only taken root

steps.title: שמואל learns it from 'when the sickle is first put'
steps.stepSummary: שמואל offers a different פסוק. The phrase מהחל חרמש implies there is grain that cannot yet be cut with a sickle, and the עומר still permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, שמואל said: The פסוק says 'from the time the sickle is first put.' Doesn't that imply there is grain that is not yet ready for the sickle?
steps.whatsHappening: Since the first source fell apart, שמואל tries a new פסוק, from the counting of the עומר. He uses the same kind of implication as before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'from when the sickle begins' implies an earlier stage, before the grain can be cut. שמואל wants that earlier stage to be grain that has only taken root.

keyTerms.meaning: A sickle, the tool used to cut grain
Fit for the sickle; ready to be cut
Rather; drops the earlier idea and brings a new one

phrases.english: Rather, Shmuel said:
"From the time the sickle is first put"

phrases.aramaic: לָאו מִכְּלָל דְּאִיכָּא דְּלָאו בַּר חֶרְמֵשׁ?
phrases.english: Does this not imply that there is grain not yet fit for the sickle?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new source after step 3 rejected the first one
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase מהחל חרמש implies there is grain not fit for the sickle that the עומר permits

steps.title: Maybe the implied grain is unripe fodder
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects שמואל's proof as well. Grain not fit for the sickle could be שחת (unripe fodder), not grain that has only taken root.
steps.simpleTranslation: It might mean grain that is not fit for the sickle but is actually שחת, unripe fodder.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on שמואל's proof in the same way it pushed back on the first one. The grain that is not ready for the sickle might be שחת, a later stage than just taking root.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again, the inference shows only that some earlier stage is permitted. שחת already has stalks, so it is far past taking root. That means the משנה's rule about rooted grain is still without a source.

keyTerms.meaning: Fodder; grain that has grown stalks but is not yet ripe

steps.confusionAlert: Both rejections work the same way. A 'not yet' inference proves that some earlier stage exists, but not that it reaches back as early as taking root.
steps.whatToRemember: Both אביב and מהחל חרמש were rejected as sources. Each inference could point to a middle stage (one-third growth or שחת) and not to grain that has only taken root.

phrases.english: It could be grain not fit for the sickle,
but it is actually fodder.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects שמואל's proof in step 4, the same way step 3 rejected step 2
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the use of מהחל חרמש as a source for the rooting rule
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The inference could refer to שחת, a stage later than taking root

steps.title: A third proof from the word 'standing grain'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק suggests that the word קמה implies there is grain too young to stand, and the עומר still permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: The פסוק says 'standing grain.' Doesn't that imply there is grain that cannot yet stand?
steps.whatsHappening: After two failed proofs, רבי יצחק offers a third פסוק to show that the עומר permits grain that has only taken root.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק counts from when the sickle is put to the קמה, the standing grain. רבי יצחק reads this as implying a weaker stage, grain that cannot stand yet, and suggests that this is the grain that has only taken root.

keyTerms.meaning: Standing grain, grain grown tall enough to stand upright
By implication, an idea learned from what the wording suggests
Able to stand, grain strong enough to stand upright

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said: "The standing grain"
Does this not imply that there is grain that is unable to stand?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After שמואל's proof is rejected, a new פסוק is offered for the same question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that the עומר permits grain that has only taken root.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word קמה implies there is grain not yet able to stand, which the עומר still permits.

steps.title: Grain that cannot stand may just be soft marsh grain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבי יצחק's proof: grain that cannot stand could be soft grain like marsh reeds, not grain that has only taken root.
steps.simpleTranslation: It could mean grain that cannot stand, but which really is soft like marsh grain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down רבי יצחק's proof, just as it rejected the two before it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inference from קמה only proves that there is some grain that cannot stand. That could be grain that has grown a fair amount but is so soft that it bends, like a marsh plant. So the פסוק does not prove anything about grain that has just taken root.

keyTerms.meaning: Marsh, here meaning soft grain that bends like a marsh plant
But really, the real case is

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the pattern: all three rejections work the same way. Each one says the implied 'weaker grain' could be a stage later than just taking root.

phrases.english: It could be grain that is unable to stand,
but it is really soft like marsh grain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from קמה offered in step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי יצחק's proof only, not the halacha itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The grain that 'cannot stand' could be soft, marsh-like grown grain rather than grain that has only taken root.

steps.title: רבא proves it from 'which you sow'
steps.stepSummary: רבא offers a new source: the פסוק אשר תזרע refers to grain from the time it is sown.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: The פסוק says 'which you sow,' meaning from the time of sowing.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the earlier proofs failed, רבא brings a different פסוק that speaks about the grain right from the sowing stage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier proofs relied on implying a 'weaker' stage, and each could be pushed off to a later stage. רבא instead uses a פסוק that directly mentions the stage of sowing, so the earliest stage of the grain is included.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, signals dropping the earlier attempts and starting fresh
Sowing, planting the seed
From the time of

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
"Which you sow" means from the time of sowing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Drops the failed approach of inferring from 'ripeness' words and brings a new type of proof.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words אשר תזרע include grain from the time of sowing.

steps.title: רב פפא: then even unrooted seed should count
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges רבא: if the פסוק counts from sowing, even seed that has not yet rooted should be permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to רבא: If so, even grain that has not taken root should be permitted too?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא objects that רבא's proof proves too much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's rule is that only grain that has taken root is permitted by the עומר. If the פסוק counts 'from sowing,' seed lying in the ground before rooting should also be included, which does not match the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, if your reasoning is right
Took root
Even though

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Rava:

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֹא הִשְׁרִישׁ נָמֵי?
phrases.english: If so, then even though it has not taken root, it should also be permitted?

steps.triggerLanguage: אי הכי אף על גב דלא השריש נמי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's proof from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reading that אשר תזרע includes grain from the moment of sowing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The proof is too broad: it would include unrooted seed, while the משנה requires that the grain has taken root.

steps.title: 'In the field' means it has rooted
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the פסוק also says בשדה, which means grain that has become part of the field by taking root.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Wise one! It is written 'in the field.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his proof by pointing to another word in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בשדה limits the sowing to grain that is truly part of the field, which happens only once it takes root. So the פסוק includes grain from the earliest point of rooting, and no earlier.

keyTerms.meaning: Wise one, a way of addressing a scholar
In the field
It is written

steps.whatToRemember: The final source is רבא's: אשר תזרע בשדה. 'Which you sow' brings in the earliest stage, and 'in the field' limits it to grain that has taken root. So the עומר permits grain that has only taken root.

phrases.english: He said to him: Wise one!
"In the field" is written.
phrases.notes: Seed only becomes part of the field once it takes root.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge from step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading another word in the same פסוק that limits the scope.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אשר תזרע includes even seed that has not yet taken root.
steps.terutzMaskana: בשדה limits it to grain that has rooted and become part of the field.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The עומר permits grain that has taken root, learned from אשר תזרע בשדה.

steps.title: New משנה: irrigated valley fields and the people of Jericho
steps.stepSummary: The משנה allows reaping irrigated valley fields before the עומר but not piling the grain. The people of יריחו reaped with the חכמים' approval and piled without it, and were not stopped.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may reap an irrigated field in the valleys, but may not pile the grain. The people of יריחו reaped with the חכמים' approval and piled without the חכמים' approval, and the חכמים did not protest.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, listing cases where reaping is allowed even before the עומר is brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reaping irrigated valley fields early is permitted, but piling the stalks into a heap is not. The people of יריחו, whose fields were this type, also piled the grain. The חכמים did not approve but did not stop them.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה, written in the text as מתני׳
An irrigated field, watered by hand or channels rather than rain
Piling the reaped stalks into a heap
With the approval of the Sages
Protested against them, stopped them

steps.confusionAlert: 'Did not protest' does not mean the חכמים agreed. The משנה clearly says the piling was against their wishes; they just did not step in.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One may reap an irrigated field in the valleys,
phrases.notes: This is talking about before the עומר, when reaping new grain is normally not allowed.

phrases.english: but one may not pile up the stalks.
The people of Jericho reaped with the approval of the Sages,
and piled the stalks without the approval of the Sages,
and the Sages did not protest against them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה after the previous discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Irrigated valley fields may be reaped before the עומר but not piled; the people of יריחו piled against the חכמים' wishes but were not stopped.

steps.title: Reaping for animal fodder: רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון disagree
steps.stepSummary: One may reap grain as fodder for animals. רבי יהודה limits this to before the grain reaches one-third of its growth; רבי שמעון allows it even after.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may reap for fodder and feed it to an animal. רבי יהודה said: When? When he begins before the grain has reached one-third. רבי שמעון says: He may reap and feed even after it has reached one-third.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds another permitted case, reaping grain to feed animals, and records a dispute about when this applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fodder is called שחת. רבי יהודה says this is only allowed if he starts before the grain reaches a third of its growth. רבי שמעון allows it even after the one-third point.

keyTerms.meaning: Unripe grain cut as animal fodder
One-third, the stage when grain has grown a third of its full growth
When? asking when the rule applies
Animal, livestock

phrases.english: One may reap for fodder and feed it to an animal.
Rabbi Yehuda said: When is this so?

phrases.aramaic: בִּזְמַן שֶׁמַּתְחִיל עַד שֶׁלֹּא הֵבִיא שְׁלִישׁ.
phrases.english: When he begins before it has reached one-third.
Rabbi Shimon says:
He may reap and feed it even after it has reached one-third.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with another permitted case of early reaping.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reaping for fodder is allowed; רבי יהודה limits it to before one-third growth, רבי שמעון allows it even after.

steps.title: Reaping for saplings, mourners, and the בית המדרש
steps.stepSummary: One may reap early to protect saplings, to make room at a house of mourning, or to make room for learning, but may not bind the grain into sheaves, only leave it in loose bunches.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may reap because of saplings, because of a house of mourning, and because of the neglect of the study hall. He may not make them into sheaves, but he leaves them in loose bunches.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists three more needs that allow reaping before the עומר, and adds a limit on how the reaped grain is handled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These cases allow reaping because of a real need: protecting young trees, making space for comforting mourners, and preventing learning in the בית המדרש from being disrupted. Even so, he may not tie the grain into proper sheaves, so it does not look like a normal harvest.

keyTerms.meaning: Saplings, young trees
House of mourning, place where mourners are comforted
Disruption of learning in the study hall
Bound sheaves
Loose bunches, stalks left untied

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה gives several cases where reaping before the עומר is allowed, but often with a limit: no piling in irrigated fields, and no binding into sheaves when reaping for a special need.

phrases.english: And one may reap because of saplings,
because of a house of mourning,
because of the neglect of the study hall.
He may not make them into sheaves,
but he leaves them in loose bunches.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of permitted early reaping.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reaping before the עומר is allowed for saplings, a house of mourning, or room for learning, but the grain may not be bound into sheaves.

steps.title: The ideal and fallback ways to harvest the עומר
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists the best way to prepare the עומר and what is still acceptable if the best way is not possible. It ends by saying the reaping overrides שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The best way is to bring the עומר from grain that is still standing in the field. If you can't find any, bring it from grain already tied in sheaves. The best way is to bring moist, fresh grain. If you can't find any, bring dry grain. The best way is to reap at night. If it was reaped by day, it is still valid. And reaping it overrides שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists three ideal ways to harvest the עומר, each with a backup that is still kosher. It ends by saying the reaping is done even on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each pair follows the same pattern: there is a preferred מצוה, but missing it does not make the עומר invalid. The last line adds that this reaping is important enough to push aside the שבת prohibition on reaping.

keyTerms.meaning: Standing grain, still attached in the field
Sheaves, grain already cut and gathered
Moist, fresh grain
Dry grain
Overrides שבת, meaning it may be done even on שבת

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up "the best way" with "required." Each fallback here (sheaves, dry grain, reaping by day) is still a kosher עומר.

phrases.english: The מצוה of the omer is to come from standing grain.
If he did not find any, he brings from sheaves.
Its מצוה is to come from moist grain;
if he did not find any, he brings dry grain.
Its מצוה is to reap at night;
if it was reaped by day, it is valid.
And it overrides Shabbat.
phrases.notes: He means the reaping of the עומר may be done even on שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה, moving from when ordinary grain may be reaped before the עומר to how the עומר itself is ideally harvested.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ideally the עומר comes from standing, moist grain reaped at night. Sheaves, dry grain, or reaping by day are still valid, and the reaping overrides שבת.

steps.title: Two phrases in one פסוק seem to clash about reaping before the עומר
steps.stepSummary: רבי בנימין points out two phrases. One suggests you reap your harvest and then bring the עומר. The other suggests the עומר must be the first of the harvest.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי בנימין says, one phrase says "and you shall reap its harvest, then you shall bring the עומר", and it is written "the first of your harvest to the כהן."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's rule that irrigated valley fields may be reaped before the עומר. It brings רבי בנימין, who sets up a tension between two phrases, so this is a setup for the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first phrase sounds like reaping may come before the עומר. The second sounds like the עומר must be the very first thing reaped. Both cannot be true in the same field, so a resolution is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that follows and explains the משנה
One phrase says, used to begin pointing out two texts that seem to clash
The first of your harvest

phrases.english: GEMARA: It is taught: Rabbi Binyamin says,
one verse says:
"And you shall reap its harvest, and you shall bring the omer",
and it is written: "The first of your harvest to the priest."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the list in the משנה and starts finding the source for the irrigated-field rule from step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two phrases conflict: one lets you reap before the עומר, the other makes the עומר the first of the harvest.

steps.title: The phrases apply to different kinds of fields
steps.stepSummary: Fields that are fit to supply the עומר may not be reaped first. Fields that are not fit, such as irrigated fields, may be reaped.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does this work? From a place you bring the עומר from, you may not reap. From a place you do not bring the עומר from, you may reap.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי בנימין resolves the clash by assigning each phrase to a different type of field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "The first of your harvest" applies to fields fit for the עומר, which are watered by rain. "Reap and then bring" applies to fields not fit for the עומר, such as irrigated valley fields. This is the source for the משנה's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: How can this be? This opens the way the two texts are reconciled
Place, here meaning a type of field

phrases.english: How is this?

phrases.aramaic: מִמָּקוֹם שֶׁאַתָּה מֵבִיא – אִי אַתָּה קוֹצֵר,
phrases.english: From a place that you bring from, you may not reap,
phrases.notes: He means a field whose grain is fit for the עומר, one watered by rain.

phrases.aramaic: מִמָּקוֹם שֶׁאִי אַתָּה מֵבִיא – אַתָּה קוֹצֵר.
phrases.english: from a place that you do not bring from, you may reap.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the tension set up in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the two phrases between two cases, here two kinds of fields
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrases seemed to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Fields fit for the עומר may not be reaped before it, while unfit fields may be.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the תורה source for the משנה's permission to reap irrigated fields before the עומר.

steps.title: Why not split by type of grain instead?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests another split: barley, which is used for the עומר, may not be reaped, but other grains such as wheat may be.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: from the type of grain you bring the עומר from, you may not reap. From a type you do not bring it from, you may reap?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי בנימין's resolution by offering another way to divide the two phrases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same pattern could be applied to grain types instead of places. Barley would be banned before the עומר, while wheat and the other grains would be allowed. That would be a very different rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead, used to suggest another reading
Type or species of grain

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא: מִמִּין שֶׁאַתָּה מֵבִיא – אִי אַתָּה קוֹצֵר,
phrases.english: Say: from the type that you bring from, you may not reap,
phrases.notes: He means barley, the grain the עומר is brought from.

phrases.aramaic: מִמִּין שֶׁאִי אַתָּה מֵבִיא – אַתָּה קוֹצֵר?
phrases.english: from the type that you do not bring from, you may reap?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the resolution in step 16 with another possible split.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי בנימין's split by place in step 16
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nothing in the wording forces a split by place. A split by grain type fits the phrases just as well.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן already showed that all five grains are included
steps.stepSummary: A split by grain type is impossible because רבי יוחנן taught that the ban on reaping before the עומר covers all five grains.
steps.simpleTranslation: You cannot say that, because of רבי יוחנן's teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the grain-type idea and so confirms that the split is by place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, on 70a, רבי יוחנן used a גזרה שוה with חלה to show that the ban before the עומר applies to all five grains. So wheat is also banned and cannot be the permitted case. The only remaining split is by type of field.

keyTerms.meaning: You cannot say that
A teaching learned from the same word appearing in two places in the Torah
The five grains: wheat, barley, spelt, oats, and rye

steps.whatToRemember: Fields fit for the עומר may not be reaped before it, but irrigated fields may. The split is by place and not by grain type, because רבי יוחנן showed all five grains are banned.

phrases.english: That you cannot say,
because of Rabbi Yochanan.
phrases.notes: This is his teaching on 70a, using חלה, that the ban before the עומר covers all five grains.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא לָא מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ, מִדְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 17 and restores the reading in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting the other option by relying on an established earlier teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe only barley is banned and other grains are allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: All five grains are banned, so the split must be by type of field.

steps.title: The משנה about the people of יריחו
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: the people of יריחו reaped with the approval of the חכמים and piled grain without their approval.
steps.simpleTranslation: The people of יריחו reap with the approval of the חכמים, and pile up grain without the approval of the חכמים, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line of the משנה so it can discuss it. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יריחו's fields were the kind that may be reaped before the עומר, so reaping there was approved. Piling the grain was a further step the חכמים did not approve. The hidden end of the line, "and they did not protest," is what the גמרא will focus on.

keyTerms.meaning: The people of the city of יריחו
They reap (cut the grain)
They pile up the cut grain into stacks
With the approval of the חכמים

phrases.english: The people of Jericho reap with the approval of the Sages,
and pile up the grain without the approval of the Sages, etc.
phrases.notes: The "etc." stands for the rest of the line in the משנה: "and the Sages did not protest against them." That ending matters for the next question.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה to discuss its next clause, after the discussion of which fields may be reaped before the עומר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In יריחו, reaping before the עומר was approved, but piling the grain was not approved, and the חכמים did not protest.

steps.title: Who talks about protesting and not protesting?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא uses the wording "they protested" and "they did not protest" about יריחו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whom have we heard say "they protested" and "they did not protest"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wants to know who wrote this part of the משנה. Its clue is the special phrase "they did not protest."
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase "did not protest" is a fingerprint. It belongs to a תנא who sorted יריחו's practices by whether the חכמים protested, not only by whether they approved.

keyTerms.meaning: They protested against them, actively objecting to what they did
Whom have you heard say this? The גמרא's way of asking which תנא holds a view

phrases.english: Whom have you heard who says
"they protested" and "they did not protest"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks who wrote the משנה line just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא uses the categories "protested" and "did not protest" for the practices of יריחו.

steps.title: It is רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the author is רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: this wording comes from רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the משנה is assigned to רבי יהודה, it must fit everything else he holds. That is what the next step will test.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage of the משנה period. Here the גמרא is identifying which one is speaking

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of who wrote the line.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי יהודה, who speaks of the חכמים protesting or not protesting.

steps.title: Does רבי יהודה really think the reaping was approved?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that this is רבי יהודה by bringing a ברייתא about six things the people of יריחו did.
steps.simpleTranslation: But does רבי יהודה hold that the reaping of the people of יריחו was approved by the חכמים? But a ברייתא teaches: The people of יריחו did six things, three with the approval of the חכמים and three without it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: it doubts that רבי יהודה would say the reaping was approved. It starts quoting a ברייתא to show why, so this step sets up the proof that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says the reaping was "with the approval of the חכמים." The גמרא suspects that רבי יהודה actually holds that none of יריחו's practices were approved. The ברייתא it begins to quote will show this.

keyTerms.meaning: And does he really hold? A challenging question
Reaping, cutting the grain
A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה
Six practices

phrases.english: But does Rabbi Yehuda hold
that the reaping of the people of Jericho
was with the approval of the Sages?
But isn't it taught in a baraita:
The people of Jericho did six things,
three with the approval of the Sages,
and three without the approval of the Sages.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה קְצִירָה דְּאַנְשֵׁי יְרִיחוֹ בִּרְצוֹן חֲכָמִים הֲוַאי? וְהָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim that the משנה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה, which calls the reaping approved, follows רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא will show that רבי יהודה considers none of יריחו's practices approved. So he cannot be the author of a משנה that calls the reaping approved.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's list of the six practices
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists three approved practices (grafting palms, running together שמע, reaping before the עומר) and three unapproved ones (piling before the עומר, using consecrated branches, opening fences for the poor on שבת). This is רבי מאיר's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: These were approved: grafting palm trees all day, running together שמע, and reaping before the עומר. These were not approved: piling grain before the עומר, permitting consecrated carob and sycamore branches, and breaking gaps in their gardens and orchards so the poor could eat fallen fruit in drought years, even on שבת and יום טוב. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues quoting the ברייתא. It lists the six practices according to רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי מאיר's version, reaping before the עומר is on the approved list, which matches our משנה. This hints that the משנה sounds like רבי מאיר, not רבי יהודה. רבי יהודה's reply comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Grafting palm trees
Running together the שמע, saying it without the usual pauses
Branches
Property consecrated to the בית המקדש
Fruit that has fallen from the tree
Years of drought

phrases.english: And these are the ones with the approval of the Sages:
they graft palm trees the entire day,
phrases.notes: He means the whole day of the 14th of ניסן, the day before פסח.

phrases.english: and they bundle the Shema,
and they reap before the omer —
with the approval of the Sages.
And these are without the approval of the Sages:
they pile up grain before the omer,
and they permit the use of consecrated branches
of carob and of sycamore trees,
and they break open gaps
in their gardens and in their orchards
to feed fallen fruit to the poor
in years of drought
on Shabbatot and Festivals,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא that the challenge quoted, giving רבי מאיר's full list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, reaping before the עומר was approved by the חכמים, and piling before the עומר was not.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: none of the six were approved
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה argues that if the חכמים had approved these practices, everyone would do them. So all six were unapproved. The only difference is that the חכמים protested three and did not protest three.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said to him: If they did these with the approval of the חכמים, then everyone would do the same! Rather, all six were done without the approval of the חכמים. For three the חכמים protested against them, and for three they did not protest.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with רבי יהודה's reply to רבי מאיר. This is the line that delivers the punch of the גמרא's challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's reasoning: something approved would not be a special custom of יריחו, because everyone would do it. So for him, reaping before the עומר in יריחו was not approved, only not protested. That clashes with our משנה, which calls the reaping "with the approval of the חכמים" yet seemed to follow רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Then everyone would do the same
Both these and those, meaning all six practices
Rather, introducing the correct version

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up "not approved" with "protested." For רבי יהודה, all six were not approved. "Did not protest" only means the חכמים let it go without objecting. So the reaping was not protested, but it was still not approved.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a real contradiction. The phrase "did not protest" points to רבי יהודה, but calling the reaping "approved" goes against him. The גמרא will need to resolve this.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said to him:
If they were doing it with the approval of the Sages,
then let every person do so!
Rather, both these and those
were without the approval of the Sages,
and about three they protested against them,
and about three they did not protest against them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: אִם בִּרְצוֹן חֲכָמִים הֵן עוֹשִׂין, יְהוּ כׇּל אָדָם עוֹשִׂין כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא by giving רבי יהודה's view. This finishes the challenge against assigning the משנה to him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, all six practices of יריחו were not approved. The חכמים protested three and did not protest three, so the reaping was not approved.

steps.title: רבי יהודה lists the three practices the חכמים did not protest
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה names the three practices the חכמים did not stop: grafting palms all day, bundling שמע, and reaping and piling before the עומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are the things the חכמים did not protest: they grafted palm trees all day, they bundled the שמע, and they reaped and piled grain before the עומר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה is filling in his list of the three practices the חכמים let the people of יריחו keep doing, even though they did not approve of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, 'did not protest' does not mean 'approved'. It only means the חכמים did not step in. Also, piling (גודשין) now sits with reaping in the not-protested group, while in רבי מאיר's version piling was one of the disapproved practices.

keyTerms.meaning: Grafting palm trees, joining a branch of one tree onto another
'Bundling' the שמע: reading it run together, without the proper pauses
Reaping, cutting the new grain
Piling the cut grain into stacks
The barley offering brought on the 16th of ניסן, before which new grain may not be eaten

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'they did not protest' as 'the חכמים agreed'. For רבי יהודה, all six practices were wrong. These three just weren't stopped.

phrases.english: And these are the ones they did not protest:
phrases.notes: This is still רבי יהודה speaking. 'Did not protest' here does not mean they approved.

phrases.english: They would graft palm trees the whole day,
and they would bundle the שמע,
and they would reap and pile before the עומר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי יהודה's statement from step 24 by spelling out which three practices were not protested.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the three practices the חכמים did not protest are grafting palms all day, bundling שמע, and both reaping and piling before the עומר.

steps.title: רבי יהודה opens the list of practices the חכמים protested
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה introduces the second list, the three practices the חכמים did protest.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these are the things the חכמים protested:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רבי יהודה is opening the list of the practices the חכמים did protest, and the items come right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since piling moved into the not-protested group, רבי יהודה's protested list must be different from רבי מאיר's disapproved list. The next lines will show what fills that third spot.

keyTerms.meaning: They protested against them, actively objected and tried to stop them
A protest or objection by the חכמים against a practice
'And these', the word that introduces a list

phrases.english: And these are the ones they protested:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the not-protested list in step 25 to the start of the protested list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opens רבי יהודה's list of the three practices the חכמים actively protested.
